chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said: I asked him about a person in Ihram who shaded himself during his Umrah.
He said: Blood (slaughter of an animal) is obligatory upon him.
He said: And if he went out to Mecca and shaded himself, it is also obligatory upon him blood for his Umrah, and blood for his Hajj.

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood (specifically, the sacrifice of an animal as a penalty)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram who shades themselves from the sun?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific penalty of 'dam' (slaughtering an animal) for a pilgrim who shades themselves during Ihram, a common act of comfort that requires expiation. The text further distinguishes the ruling for those performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj), establishing that shading in Mecca during the Hajj days incurs separate penalties for both the Umrah and the Hajj, reflecting the distinct legal statuses of each pilgrimage component in Shia jurisprudence. This highlights the precision with which Shia scholars categorize acts of worship and their corresponding compensations based on the pilgrim's specific state and location.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ali Bin Rashid who said, ‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam shading himself during his Umra.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Blood (slaughter of an animal) is Obligated upon him’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And if he goes out to Makka and shades, so it Obligates the blood (slaughter of an animal) upon him as well for his Umra, and blood (slaughter of an animal) for his Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from those whom he has mentioned from Ali ibn Rashid who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who seeks shadow in his al-‘Umrah.
He (the Imam) said, ’Slaughtering (an animal) is necessary.’
He (the Imam) then said, ‘If he goes out to Makkah and uses shadow, it is necessary to slaughter an animal; one for al-‘Umrah and one for al- Hajj.’”
